(i) **Linear and Non-Linear Elements:**
- **Linear Element:** An element whose parameters (like resistance, inductance, capacitance) do not change with voltage or current, satisfying homogeneity and additivity principles (e.g., a constant linear resistor).
- **Non-Linear Element:** An element whose parameters vary with the applied voltage or current, and do not obey superposition (e.g., diode, iron-core inductor).

(ii) **Active and Passive Elements:**
- **Active Element:** An element that delivers electrical energy to the circuit or generates power (e.g., voltage source, current source, transistor).
- **Passive Element:** An element that consumes, stores, or dissipates electrical energy but cannot generate power (e.g., resistor, capacitor, inductor).

(iii) **Unilateral and Bilateral Elements:**
- **Unilateral Element:** An element in which current flows easily in only one direction and properties change if polarity is reversed (e.g., semiconductor diode, PN junction).
- **Bilateral Element:** An element whose characteristics and current flow remain identical regardless of the direction of voltage polarity or current flow (e.g., pure resistor, inductor, capacitor).
